Literature-consistent read: The statement’s mix of “solid” growth with “some further progress” on disinflation, yet a high bar for cuts until “greater confidence,” aligns with forecast-targeting and risk-management frameworks in the modern monetary-policy literature. In Svensson and Woodford’s forecast-targeting approach, the Committee emphasizes incoming data and the balance of risks rather than pre-committing to a path, and Clarida, Galí, and Gertler’s New Keynesian policy-rule results imply holding a restrictive stance while inflation remains above target and slack is limited. The decision to keep the target range at 5.25–5.50% and continue balance-sheet runoff is consistent with Taylor-rule prescriptions and with the post-2008 floor system that uses interest on reserves and standing facilities to keep short rates firm. The slightly more “balanced” risk assessment is a dovish nuance, but ongoing QT and an explicit need for “greater confidence” before easing keep the overall tone only mildly positive. Netting these signals, the communication skews cautiously constructive on growth but still guarded on inflation.
